subject: paediatrics
title: Hypercyanotic Spells, Squatting and Transposition of Great Arteries

steps.tx: Sudden infundibular spasm acutely intensifies right-to-left intracardiac shunting into systemic circulation. In infants with tetralogy of Fallot, acute paroxysmal events termed **hypercyanotic tet spells** peak between two and six months of age. Triggers such as vigorous crying, painful procedures, defecation, dehydration, or morning awakening prompt sympathetic activation, contracting the dynamic muscular subpulmonary infundibulum and precipitating critical arterial desaturation.
steps.say: Hypercyanotic spells occur when infundibular spasm sharply cuts off pulmonary blood flow. Crying or dehydration triggers massive right-to-left shunting, causing acute hypoxia and metabolic acidosis.

vis.alt: Clinical diagrams illustrating Fallot tetralogy, infundibular spasm, and hypercyanotic spell management.
vis.caption: Infundibular muscular contraction, right-to-left shunting across VSD, and acute cyanotic spell mechanisms. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Diminished flow across the narrowed outflow tract produces a paradoxically softer heart murmur. During a hypercyanotic attack, the infant becomes deeply cyanotic, hyperpnoeic, and irritable, while auscultation reveals that the **systolic ejection murmur softens** or disappears completely. Blood is shunted away from the spastic pulmonary outflow tract right-to-left through the silent VSD into the aorta; severe spells progress to syncope, convulsions, or stroke.
steps.say: During a spell, the systolic murmur softens or disappears because blood is shunted right-to-left through the silent VSD. Deep cyanosis, rapid breathing, and limpness demand immediate therapy.

left.title: Baseline Clinic State
points: Mild cyanosis or normal pink color
Loud grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur
Stable arterial oxygen saturation (80-85%)

right.title: Acute Hypercyanotic Spell State
points: Deep, dusky, slate-blue central cyanosis
Murmur disappears or becomes barely audible
Deep acidotic hyperpnoea (Kussmaul-like)
Loss of consciousness, seizures, flaccidity

steps.tx: Compensatory postural maneuvering acutely increases systemic vascular resistance to reverse intracardiac shunting. Placing the infant in the **knee-chest position** or voluntary squatting in toddlers flexes the hips and knees, sharply kinking the femoral arteries and raising systemic vascular resistance. Elevated systemic resistance exceeds right ventricular pressure, reversing the shunt from right-to-left back to left-to-right and forcing deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary outflow tract.
steps.say: Placing the infant in a knee-chest position kinks femoral arteries and raises systemic vascular resistance. This forces blood through the pulmonary valve, immediately relieving cyanosis.

vis.alt: Clinical diagram demonstrating knee-chest positioning and evaluation of pediatric central cyanosis.
vis.caption: Knee-chest positioning increasing systemic vascular resistance during acute hypercyanotic spell resuscitation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Emergency medical therapy targets muscular relaxation, central sedation, and systemic vasoconstriction. Acute medical management of tet spells requires **subcutaneous morphine sulphate** (0.1 to 0.2 mg/kg) to sedate the child and suppress the respiratory center, high-flow oxygen, an intravenous isotonic crystalloid bolus to expand preload, intravenous sodium bicarbonate to correct metabolic acidosis, and intravenous beta-blockers like esmolol or propranolol to relax the infundibular muscle.
steps.say: Treat tet spells with high-flow oxygen, knee-chest positioning, and subcutaneous morphine. Intravenous beta-blockers relax infundibular spasm, while phenylephrine raises systemic vascular resistance.

steps.tx: Discordant ventriculoarterial connections create two separate parallel circulations incompatible with life without mixing. The most prevalent cyanotic congenital heart lesion in the immediate neonatal period is **transposition of great arteries** (d-TGA), where the aorta arises inappropriately from the morphological right ventricle and the pulmonary artery arises from the left ventricle. Systemic venous blood recirculates perpetually through the body, while oxygenated pulmonary blood recirculates uselessly through the lungs.
steps.say: In transposition of the great arteries, the aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the left. Two parallel circuits result, causing severe neonatal cyanosis on day one.

left.title: Normal Concordant Circulation
points: Systemic venous blood returns to RA -> RV -> Pulmonary Artery
Pulmonary venous blood returns to LA -> LV -> Aorta
Series circuit: 100% of blood passes through lungs and body

right.title: TGA Discordant Parallel Circulation
points: Systemic veins -> RA -> RV -> Aorta -> Body (Deoxygenated)
Pulmonary veins -> LA -> LV -> Lungs -> LA (Oxygenated)
Two separate closed parallel loops incompatible with life

steps.tx: Failure of arterial oxygenation to improve during hyperoxia testing distinguishes cyanotic heart disease from lung pathology. In d-TGA, neonates present on the first day of life with severe progressive central cyanosis unresponsive to one hundred percent oxygen, designated as a **negative hyperoxia test**. Administering pure oxygen fails to raise arterial PaO2 above one hundred millimetres of mercury because systemic desaturated blood bypasses the ventilated pulmonary bed entirely.
steps.say: A negative hyperoxia test shows arterial PaO2 failing to rise above 100 mmHg on pure oxygen. This confirms right-to-left cyanotic heart disease rather than respiratory parenchymal illness.

rows: Hyperoxia test distinguishes cardiac from lung
Cardiac neonates breathe fast without distress
Dramatic improvement in cyanosis and SpO2

steps.tx: Continuous infusion of prostaglandin preserves life-saving inter-circulatory mixing before definitive surgical repair. Suspected d-TGA requires immediate **intravenous prostaglandin E1 infusion** (alprostadil, 0.01 to 0.05 mcg/kg/min) to maintain ductus arteriosus patency, enabling mixing between pulmonary and systemic circuits. If interatrial communication is restrictive with refractory hypoxaemia, an emergency bedside balloon atrial septostomy (Rashkind procedure) is performed under echocardiographic guidance.
steps.say: Start intravenous prostaglandin E1 immediately in TGA to keep the ductus open. Bedside Rashkind balloon atrial septostomy tears the atrial septum if mixing is inadequate.

left.title: Medical Ductal Patency (PGE1)
points: Continuous infusion maintains patent ductus
Enables bidirectional mixing between great arteries
Monitor for apnoea, hypotension, and flushing

right.title: Balloon Atrial Septostomy (Rashkind)
points: Percutaneous umbilical/femoral venous access
Balloon pulled across foramen ovale to tear septum
Creates large non-restrictive interatrial shunt
Instantly elevates systemic oxygen saturation

steps.tx: Anatomical switching of the great arteries within the first weeks of life provides definitive physiological cure. The procedure of choice is the **arterial switch operation Jatene**, performed within the first two to three weeks of life before left ventricular mass regresses. The surgeon transects both great arteries, transposes the aorta to the left ventricle and the pulmonary artery to the right ventricle, and delicately relocates the coronary artery buttons.
steps.say: The arterial switch operation transposes great arteries back to their correct ventricles and transfers the coronary arteries. It must be performed within three weeks before the left ventricle regresses.

rows: Transects aorta and pulmonary artery above valves
Excises coronary buttons with surrounding aortic wall
Implants coronaries into neoaortic root (native PA)
Closes ASD and ligates patent ductus arteriosus
